STATUS: fail

SUMMARY: One reproduced blocking bug: a trailer declared in `Trailer` and set after the write leaks into the response header block, which breaks criterion 11. Compression, ServeContent, GetHead/Logger/Recoverer, ReadFrom, Flush ordering, and the concurrency and property checks all held. The probe files are deleted and `git status` is back to the starting state (README.md modified, etag.go and etag_test.go added).

FILES TOUCHED: none (probe files `middleware/zz_probe_test.go` and `middleware/zz_probe2_test.go` were created and deleted; a fix experiment ran in a scratch copy under /tmp/claude-0/scratch-redteam-etag, also deleted)

FINDINGS:
- [blocking] Late declared trailer reaches the header block. `finish` runs `maps.Copy(h, trailers)` before `ew.ResponseWriter.WriteHeader(200)`, so the value is written as a regular header. Repro: `Trailer: X-T`, `Write("tt")`, then `Header().Set("X-T","v")`. Client gets `resp.Header.Get("X-T") == "v"` (direct handler: empty). The probe failed with `late trailer X-T leaked into header block: "v"`. The existing test "declared in Trailer header, set late" misses this because it only checks `X-Late`/`X-Checksum`. In a scratch copy, moving the trailer copy after the underlying Write fixes the leak, but it breaks the existing `TestETagLateTrailersKept/http.TrailerPrefix_key_set_late`, so the fix is not a simple reorder.
- [minor] Malformed member drops well-formed members after it on the same line. `If-None-Match: "a"W/"abc"W/"a", "a"` with ETag `"a"` gives 200 instead of 304. Not reproduced as a criterion violation: the criterion says malformed members never match, and this fails in the safe direction. Found by a 20k-input property test against a naive reference.
- [minor] With `Flush` in a handler, the buffered response now carries `Content-Length` where the direct response was chunked. This is a consequence of the approved no-early-bytes difference, not a separate deviation.

CHECKS:
- `(a)` Compress inside ETag, real server, `Accept-Encoding: gzip`: decodes correctly, ETag is the hash of the encoded bytes and differs from identity, `If-None-Match` with the gzip ETag → 304 with empty body, Vary kept → pass
- `(b)` `Logger, Recoverer, GetHead, ETag`: GET and HEAD share an ETag, HEAD has no body, HEAD on empty route gets no ETag, panic → 500 with no ETag → pass
- `(c)` handler calling `http.ServeContent`: 200 gets ETag, `If-None-Match` → 304 with Last-Modified removed, `If-Modified-Since` → 304, Range → 206 with no ETag, handler-set ETag kept → pass
- `(d)` `io.Copy` from `*os.File` (32 KB), `ReadFrom`, and `io.Copy` from `strings.Reader` → identical ETag and body → pass
- Flush approved difference over a real server (handler blocked after Flush): no bytes or headers until handler returns, for flush-first, header+flush, and write+flush+flush orders → pass
- Differential, wrapped vs unwrapped, GET/HEAD/POST, 14 handler shapes (empty, small, 3000 writes, 5000 bytes, Content-Type, sniffing, 201, 204, 304, flush, trailer, Content-Length ok/bad), `inm` empty: only the trailer case differs (blocking, above) and the flush case differs as the minor item above → fail on trailer only
- Differential with `inm="*"`: 304 on every 200 path → expected per criterion 5, not a finding
- Property: 20k random If-None-Match lines against a naive reference → one mismatch (minor, above)
- Property: 1000 random chunkings of a body → ETag and body identical → pass
- `-race` on all probes → no data races
- Error wording: Hijack and Push strings match compress.go line 377/384 → pass

OPEN QUESTIONS: Should a declared trailer set after the write be dropped (as the criterion's "headers after first write don't reach the client" would imply) or sent as a trailer only? The current tests assert the trailer is sent, and only the header-block leak is the bug. The orchestrator should pick the intended behaviour before the fix.
